tools.name: list_messages
tools.description: Search the Bandwidth message log for the account (last 14 days), filtered by direction, status, type, numbers, carrier, error code, campaign or date range

message_status.description: Optional message status to filter by

message_type.description: Optional message type to filter by

source_tn.description: Optional sending telephone number in E.164 (e.g. +19195551234)

destination_tn.description: Optional receiving telephone number in E.164 (e.g. +19195551234)

carrier_name.description: Optional carrier name to filter by

error_code.description: Optional Bandwidth error code to filter by

campaign_id.description: Optional 10DLC campaign ID to filter by

from_date_time.description: Start of the receive-time range, ISO 8601 (the log only covers the last 14 days)

to_date_time.description: End of the receive-time range, ISO 8601

sort.description: Field and direction to sort by, colon separated (e.g. receiveTime:desc)

page_token.description: Pagination token returned as pageInfo.nextPageToken by a previous call

tools.name: get_message
tools.description: Look up one Bandwidth message by its message ID (delivery status, error code, carrier, timing)

message_id.description: Bandwidth message ID (the messageId returned by list_messages)

tools.name: list_media
tools.description: List the MMS media files stored in the Bandwidth account (name, size, download URL)

continuation_token.description: Continuation token from a previous call's Continuation-Token response header

needs_review: AUTH UNCHANGED from the scaffold: every Bandwidth API takes HTTP Basic with the API credential pair as username and password (their OpenAPI declares securitySchemes.Basic), which is auth.type basic + userField api_token + passField api_secret. The probe confirms the scheme: messaging.bandwidth.com answers a dummy pair with 401 and WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Realm".

account_id is a CREDENTIAL rendered into the path, not a tool input, exactly as twilio.connector.json renders account_sid. Bandwidth is account-scoped at the URL level, so there is nothing for a caller to choose and no tenant slug to guess: the shape-proof harness substitutes the dummy credential and the route still resolves.

base_url moved from dashboard.bandwidth.com (scaffolded) to messaging.bandwidth.com. This is a FORMAT constraint, not a preference: dashboard.bandwidth.com is the legacy Numbers/Account API and speaks XML for both requests and responses, while declarativeRuntime.js parses every response with resp.json(), so any tool pointed there would throw on a successful call. messaging.bandwidth.com is JSON, per Bandwidth's own OpenAPI document (bandwidth.yml in Bandwidth/python-sdk). The registry's own testEndpoint still points at the dashboard host and is untouched by this spec.

ONE HOST PER SPEC, so the voice, MFA, toll-free-verification and number-lookup surfaces are out of scope here rather than silently half-wired. Two of them are also not blind-provable: voice.bandwidth.com sits behind a Cloudflare WAF that answers EVERY path, real or bogus, with an identical 403 text/html '404 - Not Found / Request not logged', and api.bandwidth.com answered /v2/accounts/{id}/endpoints and /v2/accounts/{id}/phoneNumberLookup/bulk/{id} with 404, so those two server URLs in Bandwidth's published OpenAPI are stale.

The read surface really is this small. Bandwidth's messaging API publishes exactly three GETs (list messages, list media, download one media file) and the media download returns a binary body, so it is deliberately absent: the runtime would try to JSON-parse an image. get_message is the documented messageId filter on the same log endpoint, not a separate route.
READ-ONLY by design: no tool is marked write:true. Send message, upload media and delete media are all absent.

Response picks are documentation-derived, not data-verified: a dummy credential never yields a success body. Field names and query-parameter names come from Bandwidth's published OpenAPI (bandwidth.yml, GET /users/{accountId}/messages and GET /users/{accountId}/media), including the totalCount + pageInfo envelope and the root-array media response.

PATH PROOF IS WEAKER HERE THAN THE CLASS LABEL SUGGESTS. messaging.bandwidth.com enforces auth in front of routing: /api/v2/users/{account}/quox-bogus-subpath and /api/v2/bogus-root both answer 401 {"description":"Authentication Failed","type":"unauthorized"}, identical to the real paths. The harness control probe fires at the host root, where an AWS load balancer answers 503 rather than a 404, so the differential rests on a status difference against an infrastructure error page. Host, TLS, basic-auth handling and the credential-in-path rendering are proven by this run; the individual routes rest on Bandwidth's OpenAPI, and only a real account credential can confirm them.
